entities.summary: The Million Dollar Homepage is a website conceived in 2005 by Alex Tew, a student from Wiltshire, England, to raise money for his university education. The home page consists of a million pixels arranged in a 1000 × 1000 pixel grid; the image-based links on it were sold for $1 per pixel in 10 × 10 blocks. The purchasers of these pixel blocks provided tiny images to be displayed on them, a URL to which the images were linked, and a slogan to be displayed when hovering a cursor over the link. The aim of the website was to sell all the pixels in the image, thus generating a million dollars of income for the creator.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Million Dollar Homepage's unique concept and execution generated $1 million in revenue for its creator, Alex Tew, while also showcasing innovative online marketing strategies. Although not world-changing, it remains a notable example of entrepreneurial spirit and creative problem-solving.
